text: The reader does not read the ink alone; they breathe through the white space.
The stream does not argue with the boulder. It yields, finds the hollows, and carves the mountain.
When nothing more can be added, the work is begun. When nothing more can be removed, the vessel is complete.
The rigid pine branch snaps beneath the heavy snow. The supple willow bends until the burden falls, then springs upright unbroken.
The cracked bowl joined with gold lacquer is more honest and resilient than the porcelain that was never tested.
Do not stir the muddy pond to make it clear. Be still; the silt settles, and the mirror of the sky appears.
Before touching the wound, calm your own breathing. A restless hand cannot discern the subtle rhythm of life.
The apprentice blamed the stubborn cedar. The master inspected the apprentice's chisels: dull and nicked. 'The wood only answers the blade.'
When the archer shoots for earthenware, he shoots with ease. When he shoots for gold, his hands tremble. The skill is the same; the prize divides the mind.
Look at the weathered stone in the garden. Time did not diminish it; time revealed its true character.
Between the strike and the bell, there is motion. Between the breath and the pulse, there is stillness. Live in the interval.
When character counters dilate, the darkness cannot swallow the letters. Guard the inner light.
A scholar asked to learn Zen. The master poured tea until the cup overflowed. 'Empty your cup first, or where will the tea go?'
A finger pointing at the moon is not the moon. Do not mistake the symbol for the sky.
Nothing lasts, nothing is finished, and nothing is perfect. In this imperfection lies the dignity of the craft.
The physician listens not just to the words the patient speaks, but to the silence they hold between sentences.
Waves rise and fall, yet the ocean remains wet. Thoughts come and go, yet the mind remains open.
The felt-tip marker touches the fibrous washi. The ink bleeds slightly into the grain. In that small mark, humanity resides.
What is the highest technique? No technique. Only the right posture, the sharp blade, and the clear mind.
Before the code, the intent. During the code, the discipline. After the code, the release.
The autumn leaf falls without regret; the winter tree rests without anxiety; the spring shoot rises without boast.
Health is not the absence of storms; it is the body's natural wisdom in regaining its balance.
Slashed zero and curved l: unambiguous, humble, precise. True clarity needs no ornament.
Sitting quietly, doing nothing, spring comes, and the grass grows by itself.

A programmer out in Seattle,
Fought null-pointer bugs in a battle.
He muttered with spite,
'It worked late last night!
Now the heap starts to hiss and to rattle.'

There once was a doctor named Ned,
Whose prescription was too hard to read.
The pharmacist guessed,
'Take two for the chest!'
And cured his ingrown toe instead.

A coder who worked with CSS,
Got trapped in an infinite mess.
He tried z-index: nine,
Now the moon is offline,
And the navbar has vanished, I guess.

A patient came in feeling grey,
'I've googled my symptoms today!'
The doctor replied,
'Well, swallowing pride,
WebMD says you died yesterday.'

There once was a branch on our git,
Whose conflicts refused to submit.
With 'git push --force',
We burned down the source,
And told management, 'Tests didn't fit!'

A seagull who coded in Rust,
Declared, 'Garbage collectors are dust!
Borrow-checker is king,
I won't leak a thing—
Except sanity, which I have lost.'

A dev spent three days on a glitch,
Staring into the console's dark ditch.
He wept in despair,
Pulled out all his hair—
'Twas a semicolon out in the pitch!

My smartwatch just beeped on my wrist:
'High stress levels clearly exist!'
I yelled at the band,
'You don't understand,
My build failed and Docker is pissed!'

A typographer obsessed with the font,
Gave kerning far more than they want.
With slashed zero tight,
And curved 'l' upright,
Even stack traces look quite gallant.

An AI when asked to think deep,
Just sighed and told everyone, 'Sleep!
Your syntax is fine,
Drink water, un-whine,
Or into your coffee I'll leap!'

There are only two hard things in Computer Science:
1. Cache invalidation
2. Naming things
3. Off-by-one errors.

Why do programmers prefer dark mode?
Because light attracts bugs.

A SQL query walks into a bar, walks up to two tables, and asks:
'Can I join you?'

Doctor: 'I have good news and bad news.'
Patient: 'Give me the bad news first.'
Doctor: 'You have a severe case of acute recursion.'
Patient: 'And the good news?'
Doctor: 'I have good news and bad news.'

Why did the font break up with the paragraph?
It felt they just didn't have enough space between them.
